details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/validate_editor_audit.sh:72-80 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: non-numeric reviewers_successful values change the emitted warning literal and break downstream exact-string grep contracts.
  WHY: the branch only checks for non-empty input, so a value like "N/A" can produce a different `::warning::...` string than the numeric contract expected by the poller/tests.
- scripts/validate_editor_audit.sh:48-61 | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: the audit-section extractor and numeric parsing can truncate or mis-parse summaries and still accept malformed audits as healthy.
  WHY: the section terminator matches generic header-like or colon-terminated lines, and the follow-on field extraction does not sufficiently reject truncated or malformed audit entries.
- scripts/validate_editor_audit.sh:72-105 | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: reliance on `grep -ioP`/PCRE can make audit parsing fail open or empty on systems without PCRE support.
  WHY: on non-PCRE grep implementations the regex extraction returns empty strings, which can cause the helper to misclassify malformed audits as healthy.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12830-12961 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: the poller uses one stale comments snapshot for both noop counting and Gate B, so a new editor summary or noop-suspicious comment posted during the tick can be missed until the next cycle.
  WHY: comments are fetched once and then reused after additional API latency/redispatch logic, making validation one-cycle stale.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12930-12970 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: the tempfile write for the editor summary is unchecked, so I/O failures surface later as a misleading audit-health error.
  WHY: `printf > tempfile` can fail due to disk-full, quota, or read-only TMPDIR, but the code proceeds to validate the path anyway.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12876-12878 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: iterating `NOOP_FORCE_MERGE_SKIP_LABELS` unquoted splits multi-word labels into separate tokens and can bypass the skip gate.
  WHY: shell word-splitting breaks labels like `help wanted`, so jq exact-match checks never see the full label string.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12995-13015 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Gate D blocks on all completed failing check-runs, not only required checks.
  WHY: the API returns optional check-runs too, so an optional failure can prevent force-merge even when GitHub would allow merging.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12843-12847 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: a pagination failure while fetching comments can drop already-fetched pages and leave the sweep with an empty or incomplete comments array.
  WHY: the `--paginate` + `jq -s` pipeline falls back to `[]` on partial failure, silently skipping a PR for that cycle.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12787-12851 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: limiting the comments fetch to `per_page=100` can hide older noop-suspicious warnings on long threads.
  WHY: PRs with more than 100 comments can have relevant warnings pushed beyond page 1, so the sweep undercounts and never reaches the force-merge threshold.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:8422-8494 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: the helper is named and logs as `[conflict-dispatch]` even though it is reused for noop-recovery dispatches.
  WHY: the conflict-specific name/prefix can mislead log-based operator workflows during noop-recovery activity.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12858-12902 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: the noop-recovery sweep reuses the conflict-dispatch helper, so noop dispatches inherit conflict-specific side effects and log labels.
  WHY: the shared dispatcher is called from the noop path, which can pollute conflict-oriented logs/tracking.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12918-12920 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: malformed or `"null"` check-runs payloads can be treated like there are no failing checks.
  WHY: the jq pipeline and non-empty-string guard do not distinguish structurally invalid output from a clean array, so Gate D can incorrectly proceed.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12912-13024 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: a check can fail after the snapshot used for force-merge decisions, making the healthy-audit comment stale.
  WHY: the force-merge path is not revalidated immediately before or after scheduling `gh pr merge --auto`, so late failures can contradict the audit trail.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12766-12940 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: the sweep adds significant per-PR GitHub API load on every poll tick.
  WHY: comments/commits/pulls/check-runs requests are repeated across standalone PRs even when most are healthy, consuming rate limits.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12737 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: `NOOP_MAX_RETRIES` is hardcoded instead of being configurable like the repo's other thresholds.
  WHY: operators cannot tune the retry budget without patching the script.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12887-12893 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: jq parse errors on labels are treated the same as "label not present," so malformed label JSON can bypass the skip gate.
  WHY: the `if jq -e ...` construct only distinguishes success vs non-zero, not parse failure vs absent match.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12876-12878 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: shell word-splitting of `NOOP_FORCE_MERGE_SKIP_LABELS` can silently break multi-word opt-out labels.
  WHY: a label such as `help wanted` would be split into separate tokens that never match the full label name.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12876-12878 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: the skip-label loop is vulnerable to multi-word label splitting.
  WHY: unquoted iteration over the operator-configurable label list can cause the skip gate to miss labels containing spaces.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12876-12878 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: unquoted label iteration and related JSON handling can let skip logic behave incorrectly on malformed input.
  WHY: multi-word labels can be split apart, and malformed label payloads can be misinterpreted as simply non-matching.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/validate_editor_audit.sh:72-80 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The helper gates on non-empty `reviewers_successful`, not numeric input, so a value like `"N/A"` changes the warning literal and breaks downstream exact-string grep contracts.
  WHY: The workflow/tests expect `::warning::N reviewer(s) succeeded but...`, but the current branch emits the raw value instead of enforcing a decimal count.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:13005-13016 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Gate D filters all completed failing check-runs instead of only required checks.
  WHY: Optional failing checks can block force-merge even though GitHub's own mergeability logic would ignore them.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~12952 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Writing the temp summary file is not error-checked.
  WHY: If the write fails, the helper later sees an empty or missing file and reports a misleading audit-health failure instead of the real I/O problem.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12941 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Iterating over `NOOP_FORCE_MERGE_SKIP_LABELS` without quotes enables shell word splitting.
  WHY: A multi-word operator label would be split into multiple tokens and fail to match the intended PR label.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12876-12878 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Timestamp comparison uses bash string `<` ordering with no validation of the timestamp format.
  WHY: The comparison only works safely for ISO 8601 strings; malformed or changed formats could silently misclassify freshness.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12843-12961 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Gate B validates editor summary data from a stale comments cache.
  WHY: A new editor-summary comment posted during the poll tick can be missed until the next cycle, creating a transient false alert or delayed merge.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12843-12847 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Partial pagination failure can drop comments and leave the sweep with an incomplete array.
  WHY: If pagination fails partway through, the fallback to `[]` hides the failure and the PR can be skipped for that cycle.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:8422-8494 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `_dispatch_review_for_conflicts` and its `[conflict-dispatch]` log prefix imply conflict-specific behavior even though the function is used for noop-recovery dispatches.
  WHY: The log label and function name will confuse operators grepping for conflict-resolution activity.

=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/validate_editor_audit.sh:102-105 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The helper relies on `grep -ioP`, which can fail on systems without PCRE support.
  WHY: If PCRE grep is unavailable, the parser can fall back to empty values and incorrectly treat malformed audit data as healthy.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12876-12878 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Iterating `NOOP_FORCE_MERGE_SKIP_LABELS` with unquoted word splitting breaks multi-word labels.
  WHY: A label like `help wanted` would be split into `help` and `wanted`, so the jq match would never see the full label string.
- scripts/validate_editor_audit.sh:74 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The awk section terminator does not recognize headers with digits such as `Check 1:` or `Step 2:`.
  WHY: A future digit-containing section header could fail to terminate the audit section and let parsing bleed into following content.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12843-12960 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Gate B validates the latest editor summary from a stale comments cache instead of the freshest PR state.
  WHY: The comments are fetched once at the top of the loop and then reused, so a newly posted editor-summary comment can be missed until the next cycle.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12830-12870 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The sweep does not re-fetch PR state after a redispatch within the same cycle.
  WHY: A review run that posts a new noop-suspicious comment before the tick ends can be counted only on the next poll cycle, creating a race with the editor's merge attempt.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12968-12970 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Gate B writes and deletes the temporary summary file without checking for I/O errors.
  WHY: An unwritable TMPDIR or quota issue can make the helper see an empty summary and emit a misleading "reviewer audit unhealthy" error.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:13006-13015 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Gate D checks all completed check-runs, not just required
